answer: Each agent stakes a crystal‑valued bond before it can claim any reward; the network echoes the stake into a time‑locked forge contract that vests tokens linearly over 30 days. When a new identity registers, it must immediately lock 10 USD worth of crystal, and any premature withdrawal forfeits the full bond, making rapid Sybil scaling financially infeasible. An attacker therefore pays a fixed 10 USD per fake identity and endures a 30‑day idle period before any reward can be earned.
